steps.note: S1.3.1.1 tracks the initial side and central vectors a,c through rows 0-1, 2-5 and 6-7 and concludes the target changes by (JV+RG)x whatever a,c are, quoting line 748.
S1.3.1.2 gives the central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2, has the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one cases with 0/2 already zero, and gives self coefficient one, as at lines 752-755.
S1.3.1.3 gives the central coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2, side cancellation for intersections zero and two, zero for intersection one and self coefficient one, matching lines 756-758.
S1.3.1.4 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) using the inverse schedule X<-X-Y, with each invocation restoring its own auxiliary wires.

The plan asserts that every edge joins nested or comparable labels (S1.3.3, S1.3.3.4) and defines a residual in general (S1.3.3.6), but it never gives the per-edge orthogonal residuals or their dimensions from the table at lines 1022-1042.

S1.3.3.3 states the inclusion <t_X> ⊂ t_Y^⊥ from t_X⊥t_Y (quoting the label construction at line 953), but it never gives the 2->5 residual <t_X,t_Y>^⊥ or its dimension h-2, which is the content of lines 1056-1058.

The plan names the center 3->4 edges as the only decreasing ones, each losing h (S1.3.3.4), gives source sum N and sink sum Wm-N (S1.3.3.2), telescopes at the gates to signed Wm-2N, and adds 2L for absolute values (S1.3.3.5).

S1.3.3.6 states that over F_2 every nonzero residual contains a norm-one vector, so it is nonalternating (and nondegenerate) and therefore has an orthonormal basis; it attributes nondegeneracy loosely and omits the absorption of alternating planes, but the step's reasoning is there.
S1.3.3.7 states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 exactly.
S1.3.5.1 gives wt(z+w)=wt(z)+wt(w)-2|supp∩supp|, concludes additivity mod 4 when z·w=0, and writes q_V-q_U as one term wt(v)[v·x] per orthonormal basis vector of the residual.
S1.3.5.2 uses the odd weight to get the phase i^{±[v·x]} with its two-term expansion and applies H diag(1,-1) H = X to obtain aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The plan counts s_c child calls on the f bits of one slot (S1.5.1, S1.5.1.1), but it never states that the frame on several columns is the tensor power of C_U, so that each residual vector's kernel tensors into one factor acting on all columns; it asserts the count without the tensoring step.

S1.5.1.5 lists the corrections (source and sink Z signs, the scalar i^{27f}, negating the X bank), but it never says what they repair: the zero label has frame I, the full label has frame C^{⊗m}, and C^{-1} sits on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) on X_a->Y_a, fixed via C=iZC^{-1}Z. S1.5.1.3 uses the Z-conjugation identity only for inverse children.
The plan states both ratios are below 1/2 (S1.3.3.7), derives the deficits N-2L_b>0 (S1.3.4.3) and 2N-2L_c>0 (S1.3.5.3), and hence s<Wm for both networks.
S1.3.6 has both deficits above 20·2^{-50} and log m<20 from m<2^20, so m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20·2^{-50}) and s_b/W_b<m^τ, s_c/W_c<m^σ with τ=σ=1-2^{-50}, quoting line 1331.

S1.3.7.1 eliminates from the topmost nonzero row with its rightmost nonzero pivot using only lower-triangular operations, isolating one rank-one block per step, which gives A=E_1ΠE_2 with exactly a ones in Π.

S1.3.7 only says in a parenthetical that q is 'a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators'; it never mentions the finite table of factors and inverses, or that the rational identities specialize to Z/q^b with the triangular factors still invertible.
S1.3.7.2 states that a lower-triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order from earlier, still unchanged coordinates.
S1.3.7.3 realises each one of Π at (i,j) as D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange of (H_i,D_j), then D_j<-H_i-D_j, so there are exactly a recursive interchanges.
The plan gives E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E and m^10<B<m^11 (S1.5.4.1), Δ=⌈C_0 d^{20}⌉ (S1.5.4) and C_1=20 (S3.5.1), but it never defines C_0=128mB^2, ν, or C_1=max{20,ν+3}, so Δ is left undetermined.
The S1.5.4 method states A(e)≤sA(e/m)+E, and S1.5.4.1 has each invocation add at most E=64(W+m+1)^3 operations and leaves need at most 8e.

S1.5.4.1 states the result 'depth at most 8B^2d^{12}' and quotes line 2525, but it omits the unrolling B^{k+1}≤B^2 d^ν over k≤⌈log_m d⌉ levels and never bounds the total (pieces and outer phases) below C_0 d^{C_1}.
S1.5.4.2 places depth-ℓ values in 2^{-(p+ℓ)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^ℓ and reserves p+Δ fractional and Δ+3 integer bits; S1.5.4.3 uses 20ε<1 (εC_1<1 with C_1=20) to get Δ=o(p).
S1.5.5 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and the single final truncation errs by less than √2·2^{-p}, quoting line 2752.

summary: P01 carries 19 of the 26 sub-steps. All of the bank exchange (B1-B4), rank saving (R1-R4) and simultaneous-layer recurrence and guard bits (S2, S4, S5) are present, as are the telescoping, orthonormal-basis and ratio steps of the label budget (L3-L5), the phase factorization (P1-P2) and the shear elimination, triangular cost and interchange (M1, M3, M4). The seven absent sub-steps are cases where the plan asserts a result without its mechanism: no per-edge residual table (L1); no 2->5 residual <t_X,t_Y>^⊥ of dimension h-2 (L2); no column-tensoring step (P3); no endpoint frames I and C^{⊗m} or C^{-1} on supp(u_a) (P4); no prime-specialization argument (M2); no definition of C_0 (S1); and no unrolling B^{k+1}≤B^2d^ν or total below C_0 d^{C_1} (S3). No sub-step is stated contrary to the paper.
